statement: Express $3\\cos x+4\\sin x$ in the form $R\\cos(x-\\alpha)$ with $R>0$ and $0<\\alpha<\\tfrac{\\pi}{2}$. Hence find its maximum value and solve $3\\cos x+4\\sin x=2$ for $x\\in[0,2\\pi)$.
solution: $3\\cos x+4\\sin x=R\\cos(x-\\alpha)=R(\\cos x\\cos\\alpha+\\sin x\\sin\\alpha)$, so $R\\cos\\alpha=3$, $R\\sin\\alpha=4$, giving $R=5$ and $\\tan\\alpha=\\tfrac43$ ($\\alpha=\\arctan\\tfrac43$). Maximum value is $5$. For $=2$: $5\\cos(x-\\alpha)=2\\Rightarrow \\cos(x-\\alpha)=\\tfrac25$, so $x-\\alpha=\\pm\\arccos\\tfrac25$, giving two solutions in $[0,2\\pi)$.
